section: National Commission for SCs (338), STs (338A) and Backward Classes (338B); Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (350B)
subsections: Backward Classes Commissions → chairman, year, government
Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC

accepted.s:
With reference to the National Commission for Women, consider the following statements:
1. It is a statutory body.
2. It was created under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.
3. It was constituted in 1992.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The NCW is statutory, derives its authority from the 1990 Act and was constituted in 1992.
accepted.tq: Check whether the question distinguishes the year of the Act from the year of constitution.

accepted.s: The First Backward Classes Commission was appointed in which year, and its report was submitted in which year?
accepted.x: The First Backward Classes Commission was appointed in 1953 and submitted its report in 1955. It was headed by Kaka Kalelkar.
accepted.tq: Separate the appointment year from the report year instead of treating them as the same date.
accepted.sec: Backward Classes Commissions → chairman, year, government

accepted.s: The recommendation of 27 per cent reservation for Other Backward Classes was implemented by which government in 1990?
accepted.x: The Mandal Commission recommended 27 per cent reservation for OBCs, and the recommendation was implemented by the V.P. Singh government in 1990.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the government that appointed a commission from the government that implemented its recommendation.
accepted.sec: Backward Classes Commissions → chairman, year, government

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes:
1. Each Commission consists of a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three members.
2. All members are appointed by the President by warrant.
3. Their service conditions and tenure are fixed by the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Each Commission has five members in all, appointed by the President by warrant, with service conditions and tenure fixed by the President.
accepted.tq: Verify composition, appointing authority and service conditions independently before selecting the coded option.

accepted.s: Under the applicable rules, the tenure of the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and members of the NCSC and NCST is:
accepted.x: The term of office of the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and members is three years under the applicable rules.
accepted.tq: Focus on the precise numerical term rather than confusing it with the term of another constitutional office.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the rank associated with offices in the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
o: Chairperson—Union Cabinet Minister; Vice-Chairperson—Minister of State; members—Secretary rank
Chairperson—Minister of State; Vice-Chairperson—Secretary rank; members—Cabinet Minister rank
Chairperson—Secretary rank; Vice-Chairperson—Cabinet Minister; members—Minister of State rank
Chairperson—Chief Minister; Vice-Chairperson—Cabinet Secretary; members—Joint Secretary rank
accepted.x: The Chairperson of the NCST has the rank of a Union Cabinet Minister, the Vice-Chairperson has the rank of a Minister of State, and the members have Secretary rank.
accepted.tq: Match each office with its designated rank, taking care not to reverse the hierarchy.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the National Commission for Backward Classes is correct?
o: Its constitutional composition consists of a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three members.
It continues to have only the five-member composition of the 1993 statutory body.
It is headed by a retired Supreme Court or High Court judge as a constitutional requirement.
Its members are appointed by the Central Government without presidential involvement.
accepted.x: The constitutional NCBC consists of a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three members appointed by the President. The earlier statutory NCBC had five members and was headed by a retired Supreme Court or High Court judge.
accepted.tq: Separate the present constitutional NCBC from the earlier five-member statutory NCBC.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to the National Commissions in chronological order:
A. Creation of non-statutory commissions by government resolutions
B. Replacement of the Special Officer by a multi-member constitutional commission
C. Bifurcation into the NCSC and NCST
D. Creation of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs
accepted.x: The correct order is A (1978 and 1987), B (1990), D (1999), and C (2003, followed by implementation in 2004).
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the dated constitutional amendments and place the 1999 ministry between them.

accepted.s: The 65th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1990 is associated with which development?
o: Replacement of the Special Officer for SCs and STs by a multi-member National Commission
Bifurcation of the NCSC into the NCSC and NCST
Restoration of the States’ power to prepare SEBC lists
Creation of the constitutional NCBC under Article 338B
accepted.x: The 65th Amendment, 1990 replaced the Special Officer for SCs and STs with a multi-member constitutional National Commission. The NCBC was constitutionalised by the 102nd Amendment, while bifurcation occurred through the 89th Amendment.
accepted.tq: Match the amendment with its precise institutional change rather than a later development.

accepted.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes became operational with effect from:
accepted.x: The NCST was set up with effect from 19 February 2004 following the bifurcation authorised by the 89th Constitutional Amendment.
accepted.tq: Test the exact operational date separately from the year of the constitutional amendment.

accepted.s: Which development provided the contextual basis for creating a separate commission for Scheduled Tribes?
o: Creation of the Ministry of Social Justice in 1990
The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
The National Commission for Women Act, 1990
Creation of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs in 1999
accepted.x: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs was created in 1999, a development that preceded and supported the establishment of a separate commission for Scheduled Tribes.
accepted.tq: Link the institutional development with the ministry specifically concerned with tribal affairs.

accepted.s: In Indra Sawhney v. Union of India, decided on 16 November 1992, the Supreme Court, among other things, upheld:
o: 27 per cent reservation for OBCs and the concept of the creamy layer
50 per cent reservation exclusively for economically weaker sections
The abolition of all reservation in public employment
The exclusive power of States to notify all SEBCs without constitutional limitation
accepted.x: The judgment upheld 27 per cent reservation for OBCs, introduced the creamy-layer principle and directed the creation of a permanent body concerning inclusion and exclusion from the OBC list.
accepted.tq: Combine the date with the judgment’s distinct holdings instead of confusing it with later amendments.
accepted.sec: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC

accepted.s: The income ceiling associated with the creamy layer, as notified in 2017, is:
accepted.x: The creamy-layer income ceiling mentioned in the relevant notification is ₹8 lakh per year. Andhra Pradesh aligned its definitions with the central thresholds.
accepted.tq: Compare the closely spaced monetary figures and select the notified threshold.
accepted.sec: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the effect of the 102nd and 105th Constitutional Amendments in relation to SEBCs?
o: The 102nd Amendment created the creamy layer, while the 105th Amendment abolished it.
The 102nd Amendment gave the President power to notify SEBCs, while the 105th Amendment restored the States’ power to prepare their own lists.
The 102nd Amendment restored State lists, while the 105th Amendment gave the President the first power to notify SEBCs.
Both amendments abolished the power of the President to notify SEBCs.
accepted.x: The 102nd Amendment enabled the President to notify SEBCs. The 105th Amendment, 2021 restored the States’ power to prepare their own SEBC lists.
accepted.tq: Compare the two amendments by assigning one distinct constitutional effect to each.
accepted.sec: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the statutory National Commission for Backward Classes:
1. It was established under the NCBC Act, 1993.
2. The Act came into force on 2 April 1993.
3. It had five members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The statutory NCBC was established under the 1993 Act, which came into force on 2 April 1993, and it had five members.
accepted.tq: Check the Act, commencement date and composition as separate components of the earlier statutory body.
accepted.sec: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC

accepted.s: The direction in Indra Sawhney concerning a permanent body for inclusion and exclusion from the OBC list led to the establishment of the:
o: National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under the 89th Amendment
National Commission for Women under the 1990 Act
Statutory National Commission for Backward Classes under the 1993 Act
National Commission for Minorities under the 1992 Act
accepted.x: The direction in Indra Sawhney led to the NCBC Act, 1993 and the establishment of the statutory NCBC. It was intended to advise on inclusion and exclusion from the OBC list.
accepted.tq: Trace the judicial direction to the institution created to perform the specified function.
accepted.sec: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a consequence of the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018?
o: Bifurcation of the NCSC and NCST
Insertion of Article 338B and constitutional status for the NCBC
Insertion of Article 350B and creation of the Linguistic Minorities Officer
Creation of the first statutory NCBC
accepted.x: The 102nd Amendment inserted Article 338B and gave constitutional status to the NCBC. The other developments belong to different constitutional provisions or earlier enactments.
accepted.tq: Match the amendment with its article and institutional result, avoiding chronology traps.
accepted.sec: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC

accepted.s: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment also had the effect of:
o: Transferring all SEBC-list powers to State Governors
Removing Scheduled Tribes from the purview of the NCST
Removing backward classes from the purview of the NCSC
accepted.x: The 102nd Amendment removed backward classes from the purview of the NCSC while constitutionalising the NCBC under Article 338B.
accepted.tq: Look for the precise change in jurisdiction rather than a general statement about reservation.
accepted.sec: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Commission for Minorities:
1. It is a statutory body under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992.
2. The first statutory National Commission for Minorities was constituted in 1993.
3. The Chairperson and members are appointed by the President of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the Chairperson and members of the NCM are appointed by the Central Government, not by the President.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who appoints?’ trap, especially where a constitutional President may be confused with the Central Government.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the composition of the National Commission for Minorities after the 1995 amendment?
o: A Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and five members
A Chairperson and three members only
A Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three members
A Chairperson, two Vice-Chairpersons and four members
accepted.x: The 1995 amendment added a Vice-Chairperson, resulting in a total of seven members: a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and five members.
accepted.tq: Calculate the total composition after identifying the amendment’s specific addition.

accepted.s: Under Section 3(2) of the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, at least how many members including the Chairperson must belong to minority communities?
accepted.x: Five members, including the Chairperson, must be from minority communities under Section 3(2) of the Act.
accepted.tq: Read the qualifying phrase ‘including the Chairperson’ carefully before selecting the number.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the National Commission for Minorities is correct?
o: It has a five-year term and exercises criminal court powers in all matters.
It has a one-year term and no inquiry powers resembling those of a civil court.
It has a six-year term and is constituted by a constitutional amendment.
It has a three-year term and exercises civil court powers during inquiries.
accepted.x: The NCM has a three-year term and exercises civil court powers during inquiries. It is a statutory body under the 1992 Act, not a constitutional body.
accepted.tq: Separate the duration of tenure from the nature of inquiry powers and the body’s legal status.

accepted.s: Which of the following was the precursor to the statutory National Commission for Minorities?
o: The 1993 Protection of Human Rights Act
The 1990 National Commission for Women Act
A 1978 resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs
A 1987 resolution of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs
accepted.x: The Minorities Commission created by a 1978 Ministry of Home Affairs resolution was the precursor to the statutory NCM established under the 1992 Act.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the precursor executive resolution from the later statutory enactment.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs of communities is NOT included among the notified minority communities?
accepted.x: The notified minority communities are Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains. Jews are not included in this listed group.
accepted.tq: Find the outsider in a recognised statutory list rather than choosing a community from memory alone.

accepted.s: Who was appointed Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities for a three-year term in 2026?
accepted.x: Harjit Singh Grewal was appointed Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities for a three-year term in 2026.
accepted.tq: Match the current appointee with the correct statutory commission and tenure.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis:
1. It was created by the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis Act, 1993.
2. The Act lapsed in 2004.
3. The Commission continues as a non-statutory body with its tenure extended by resolution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The NCSK was created under the 1993 Act; after the Act lapsed in 2004, it continued as a non-statutory body through tenure extensions by resolution.
accepted.tq: Track the transition from statutory creation to present non-statutory continuation.
